title: Distinguish transformer families, pretraining and adaptation, inference context, and sparse-expert routing without equating fluent output with verified reasoning

questions.prompt:
A code editor needs an autocomplete feature. It extends partly typed code by generating one token at a time, left to right. There are two pretrained candidate models of similar size:

- **Model A:** a GPT-style decoder-only transformer.
- **Model B:** a BERT-style encoder-only transformer.

Explain why Model A can do this task and why Model B cannot do it on its own. For **each** model, describe its **attention pattern** and its **pretraining objective**, and say how each one affects left-to-right generation.

rubric.point: Model A's attention: causal (masked) attention, so each position attends only to earlier tokens. This matches generating left to right.
Model A's pretraining objective: next-token prediction. This is the same task as continuing a prompt one token at a time.
Model B's attention: bidirectional, so every token attends to the whole input on both sides. It produces contextual representations of an existing input, not a continuation.

Model B's pretraining objective: masked-token prediction from context on both sides. It fills gaps inside a given input and has no autoregressive decoder, so it cannot generate open-ended text on its own.

questions.model:
**Model A** uses causal attention, so each token sees only earlier tokens. This matches left-to-right generation. It is pretrained on next-token prediction, which is the same task as extending code one token at a time.

**Model B** uses bidirectional attention over the whole input, so it builds contextual vectors for text that already exists. It is pretrained to predict masked tokens from context on both sides. That teaches it to fill gaps, not to continue text, and it has no autoregressive decoder for generation.
